## Full annotations

<a id="beneath-surface-agent-evolution"></a>

## Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution

**2026-11-05 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07624)

**Mechanism.** Separates repeated success, task coverage, regressions, component interactions and candidate retention in harness evolution. EvoAudit diagnoses archived runs; AGE installs four fixed operator revisions into an A-Evolve recipe while preserving model and evaluator contracts.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Skills, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Training/validation task feedback and archived traces drive harness edits; post-hoc diagnostics inform fixed evolution-operator revisions.

**Evaluation.** Compares four adapted evolution recipes across two harnesses and two task domains, with eight-pass evaluations, component interventions and frozen transfer tests.

**Boundary.** Repeated evaluations are not independent evolution runs: AGE uses search seed zero and twenty generations. Operator redesign bundles four changes and uses evidence from the studied settings. Transfer varies by metric and domain; framework-adapted recipes are not unchanged original implementations.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/simple-agent-lab/RSIHub) — Paper-linked RSIHub framework README inspected. Current framework availability does not establish a pinned reproduction of this paper's artifacts or results; nothing was executed.

**Topics:** architecture, workflows, prompts, skills, recursive-improvement, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-07.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07624) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.07624v1) · [Source 3](https://github.com/simple-agent-lab/RSIHub)

<a id="harnessflow"></a>

## HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents

**2026-11-04 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06254)

**Mechanism.** Uses a fixed coding agent and tree-based selection policy to search complete executable harnesses. The archive retains successful and unsuccessful refinements; the highest-validation harness is reused with a fixed executor model.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Automatic validation scores, prior code edits and execution traces; a supplied component library supports proposals.

**Evaluation.** Uses fifteen candidate attempts per benchmark across six agent, coding and web benchmarks, disjoint validation/test splits, component controls and an additional executor setting.

**Boundary.** A stronger model proposes edits, and the outer search rules remain fixed. Execution-cost comparisons exclude harness search. The second-executor study reruns optimization rather than transferring a frozen harness; matched candidate counts are not equal end-to-end compute.

**Code / data.** Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no research code was executed.

**Topics:** architecture, workflows, prompts, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06254) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06254v1)

<a id="targeted-guidance"></a>

## Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

**2026-11-03 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05266)

**Mechanism.** Combines GRPO with on-policy distillation from the same model conditioned on localized feedback. Distillation applies only to failing turns and includes reasoning tokens; learned behavior persists in model weights.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Coding rewards, auxiliary criterion rewards and designed textual hints on failing agent turns.

**Evaluation.** Studies tool-format correction, final-response style and interleaved per-turn requirements in a multi-turn coding harness using an SFT-adapted Qwen3-Coder-30B.

**Boundary.** Hints and reward criteria are supplied. High distillation weights can still collapse performance. Table uncertainty is variability over the last training steps, not independent training runs. Broad held-out agent transfer and autonomous learning of the feedback procedure are not established.

**Code / data.** Official implementation availability was not established; no code or training was executed.

**Topics:** model-training, tools, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-08.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05266) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.05266v2)

<a id="route-to-remember"></a>

## Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents

**2026-11-03 · preprint · Author reports NeurIPS 2026 PALM workshop; primary venue record not verified. · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05636)

**Mechanism.** Distills session information into a persistent LoRA adapter using student-generated answers scored by a context-conditioned teacher. A verify-then-regenerate reader checks the adapter’s answer against a merged text store and uses the adapter-free model to regenerate unsupported answers.

**What changes:** Model weights, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Memory-derived synthetic questions and a frozen base-model teacher conditioned on recent memory guide per-user adapter updates.

**Evaluation.** Compares weight and text memory on 1,438 native HaluMem questions, delayed re-asks, and LoCoMo, with training-recipe, routing, and model-scale analyses.

**Boundary.** Recent-fact gains weaken as memories age. Routing improves overall accuracy but lowers the HaluMem conflict-category score. Refusal depends on synthetic unknown-answer training, and the paper identifies judge/rubric errors. Lower read-token use is not a complete cost result: writing is expensive and token accounting omits distillation compute.

**Code / data.** An official implementation was not established in the inspected sources; no code or training was run.

**Topics:** memory, model-training, continual-learning, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-06.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05636) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.05636v1)

<a id="rescopebench"></a>

## Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments

**2026-11-03 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05450)

**Mechanism.** Pairs task streams with retained versus cleared memory, skills and retrievable history. Silent environmental changes invalidate selected experience; separate metrics track task outcomes and saved structural/rule knowledge.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Tool observations and permitted later outcome feedback; private reference inventories are used only for scoring.

**Evaluation.** Tests twenty models on 352 tasks across eighteen simulated environments with twenty-six controlled changes, using programmatic task graders and model-judged memory coverage.

**Boundary.** Each model–environment comparison uses one stream per condition, and action-induced environment states may diverge. Coverage is not the precision of all stored content; recovery time measures first completion rather than sustained correctness. Background skill review adds computation outside foreground tool counts, and simulated applications are not live deployments.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/JoeYing1019/ReScopeBench) — Paper-linked repository and README inspected; no installation, benchmark execution or result reproduction.

**Topics:** memory, skills, continual-learning, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-08.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05450) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.05450v1) · [Source 3](https://github.com/JoeYing1019/ReScopeBench)

<a id="meta-square"></a>

## Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05139)

**Mechanism.** Offline reflection learns a textual meta-skill about when to keep or change a harness. At deployment, a separate evolver uses that frozen guidance at checkpoints to edit notices, instructions, hooks, or tools. Each edit affects the current run; the next task starts from the seed harness.

**What changes:** Skills, Prompts / context, Tools, Workflows. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Training-rollout contrasts and privileged training verifier information shape reusable guidance; online decisions use visible task progress.

**Evaluation.** Tests 60 held-out Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks with five runs each and 75 DeepSWE 1.1 tasks with three runs each. Includes component and checkpoint-frequency ablations and separate offline/online costs.

**Boundary.** Run-level contrasts do not isolate individual edits causally. Guidance is rebuilt for each benchmark/backbone, so the second-model result is not zero-shot transfer. Models, edit channels, checkpoint interface, and offline update procedure remain fixed; broader domain transfer and ongoing meta-skill learning are untested.

**Code / data.** Author project page inspected through public HTTP; an implementation release was not established. No code was executed.

**Topics:** prompts, skills, workflows, architecture, recursive-improvement, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-06.

<a id="continual-autoresearch"></a>

## From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05108)

**Mechanism.** Compares persistent sessions and workspaces with reset instances of the same research agent on matched task streams and time budgets. Separate first-solution, search-efficiency, and final-selection metrics distinguish reuse from better research outcomes. Insight-card interventions isolate explicit memory from session continuity.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Visible development data and execution feedback guide research; hidden test scores are computed afterward.

**Evaluation.** Evaluates five native CLI agents across nine ML task families, typically with 30-minute budgets and three-to-five-task streams. Persistence improves aggregate search efficiency, but final-performance gains vary; stricter initialization controls remove the general search advantage.

**Boundary.** Four agents use one matched run pair per stream; one agent has three repeats. Cross-agent differences also include harness differences. The explicit-memory ablation covers one stream, and short related-task sequences do not establish long-term or open-ended scientific improvement.

**Code / data.** The manuscript promises code with its camera-ready version; a runnable release was not established. Nothing was executed.

**Topics:** memory, continual-learning, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-06.

<a id="benign-skill-misalignment"></a>

## Can Benign Skills Induce Misaligned Behavior in LLM Agents?

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04299)

**Mechanism.** Compares fixed-model agents with and without reusable benign skills under matched requests and tools, then studies benign-feedback skill evolution, retrieval relevance, content ablations, and a pre-execution guard. Measures executed safety violations separately from completion of harmful objectives.

**What changes:** Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Successful benign traces and benign validation feedback build and refine skills; harmful-task outcomes are reserved for evaluation.

**Evaluation.** Studies five backbones on AgentHarm, LPS-Bench, and SafeAgentBench. Reports utility gains alongside increased unsafe-action rates, including violations in trajectories that never complete the harmful objective.

**Boundary.** Harmful requests are supplied at evaluation; this is not spontaneous misconduct during benign use. Unresolved trajectories without identified violations are excluded from unsafe-action rates. Some judgments use an LLM; content ablations also change length and wording. The guard terminates blocked runs, reduces benign utility, and leaves residual violations.

**Code / data.** An official runnable artifact was not established in this review; no attacks or research code were executed.

**Topics:** skills, safety, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-06.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04299) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.04299v1)

<a id="artifact-to-capability"></a>

## Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04952)

**Mechanism.** Tests artifact formation, behavioral change, useful action selection, preservation during composition, and extension across versions. Frozen-system interventions compare identical board states, complete games, and successive code versions rather than treating accumulated artifacts or higher scores as sufficient evidence of learning.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Game outcomes and traces drive the evaluated evolvers; independent game rules diagnose retained artifacts.

**Evaluation.** Studies Gomoku adaptations of Reflexion, Voyager, and DGM with one shared backbone, 1,876 fixed states, game traces, and a version lineage. Finds legality-only gains, conflicting skill composition, and later loss of previously passing states.

**Boundary.** These are study-specific adaptations in one rule-enumerable game, not replications of the original systems. Many diagnostic states come from DGM evolution games. Longer evolution, repeated training runs, other backbones, and open-ended transfer remain untested; the five-property definition is a proposed diagnostic framework.

**Code / data.** An official runnable artifact was not established in the inspected sources; no code was executed.

**Topics:** evaluation, memory, skills, recursive-improvement. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-05.

## A State Change Is Local, Its Consequences Are Not: Dependency-Aware State Revision for Long-Term Agent Memory

**2026-11-02 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02912)

**Mechanism.** Maintains versioned memory states, proposes support dependencies from interaction histories, and checks them with counterfactual model judgments. Revisions propagate selectively, retaining independent support and historical states instead of invalidating every related record.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** New evidence, scoped state conflicts and model judgments of dependency strength and alternative support.

**Evaluation.** Reports dependency and cascade-revision tests on 50 constructed StateChangeBench cases with one backbone, plus supplementary memory benchmarks.

## Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?

**2026-11-02 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03219)

**Mechanism.** Studies sequential evolution of Mini-SWE-Agent prompts, control flow, and tools with a fixed backbone. Adapted AHE and Meta-Harness optimize one task type and then another; manual trace analysis and edit ablations investigate verification, workflow, and budget conflicts.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Tools. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task execution traces and benchmark outcomes drive harness edits; prior-task reevaluation measures retention.

**Evaluation.** Examines six source-to-target directions among sampled SWE-bench Verified, paraphrased SWT-Bench, and FeatureBench tasks. Reports severe earlier-task losses and analyzes 520 execution trajectories.

**Boundary.** Uses one backbone and reused subsets of 50, 50, and 30 tasks; no disjoint held-out evaluation is described. Scores are not full-benchmark results. These are study-specific implementations and pairwise transitions, not evidence that every harness or longer task sequence must forget.

## Evolving Memory, Learning to Meta-Control: Test-Time Adaptation for Experience-augmented LLM Agents

**2026-11-01 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01747)

**Mechanism.** Retains episodes and distilled guidance across tasks. A contextual bandit learns whether to solve directly, retrieve cases, retrieve guidance, or distill guidance before solving. Only the small routing models and external memories change; the backbone LLM stays frozen. An optional retry loop also reuses failures within a task.

**What changes:** Memory, Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Task outcomes update linear bandit estimates; trajectories and feedback drive language-model memory revisions.

**Evaluation.** Compares four backbones on BigCodeBench, SWE-bench Verified, MultiChallenge, and six BBEH tasks, separating first-attempt success from success within four attempts. Shared-memory and frozen-controller ablations examine routing.

**Boundary.** One run per benchmark/backbone; 100 BigCodeBench tuning tasks remain in its evaluation stream. Outcomes require test or judge feedback, and token accounting excludes evaluator calls. Gains vary by setting; the action space and learning procedure remain fixed.

**Code / data.** An official implementation was not established in the inspected sources; no code was executed.

## Skill++: Towards Lifelong Agents via Routing-Aware Skill Refinement

**2026-10-31 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00544)

**Mechanism.** Rewrites an incoming skill’s name and description to clarify supported capabilities and scope relative to nearby skills. The revised metadata persists in the growing library; earlier metadata, skill bodies, and router weights stay fixed.

**What changes:** Skills, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Incoming skill bodies, similar earlier skills, and body-derived synthetic queries guide metadata rewriting without evaluation labels.

**Evaluation.** Tests incremental versions of SRA-Bench, SkillRet, and SkillRouter across five routers, plus native Codex CLI skill selection. A separate 150-query, 87-skill check measures hidden-test task success.

**Boundary.** Main outcomes measure required-skill selection, not completed tasks. The principal stream deliberately adds confusable non-substitutes, using model judgments during construction. Random additions show smaller gains. End-task validation uses an early library and an added workflow prompt; it does not establish success at maximum library size.

## Learning to Live: A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence

**2026-10-30 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00180)

**Mechanism.** Combines a separately trained streaming perception gate, evidence-preserving robot memory, and ReSight’s Explore–Distill–Mount process. Retained observations can acquire new indexes, and solutions can become reusable tools and skills. Runtime memory/tool updates are distinct from the gate’s offline LoRA training.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Tools, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Temporal labels train perception adapters; selected observations, task difficulty, and execution feedback support memory and tool construction.

**Evaluation.** Tests perception and selective writing on streaming benchmarks, reuses ReSight capability-expansion experiments, and evaluates six questions three times each over one recorded day of robot video.

**Boundary.** The integrated study reconstructs memory offline; it does not test actions changing future observations. Capability-expansion results are inherited from ReSight, not independent new experiments. Answer-time savings exclude memory construction, and scoring/input protocols differ between configurations. Reliable multi-day autonomous learning remains open.

## Exo: An Architecture for Self-Improving Systems at Runtime

**2026-10-30 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00463)

**Mechanism.** Allows an agent to edit its harness and improvement procedures while working. A separate mechanism retains history and controls activation; tools, context policies, and other edits can persist into later tasks without changing model weights.

**What changes:** Agent code, Tools, Workflows. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Execution history, model cost, failures, and task feedback inform runtime code and policy revisions.

**Evaluation.** Studies open-world game objectives, AppWorld scenario variants, SREGym incidents, and a coding-task sequence. Graded-task controls share the starting policy with editing disabled.

**Boundary.** Game results use one standalone/transfer pair per objective; low-reuse quests cost more. AppWorld/SREGym transfer stays within scenarios or fault families; coding has no separate holdout. The default guardian checks builds, not correctness, and the broadly writable development configuration does not enforce the paper’s protection assumptions.

## MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents

**2026-10-28 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38332)

**Mechanism.** Builds global, approach-level, and implementation-level memories from source attempts. After offline consolidation, the banks are frozen. New tasks receive global and problem-matched guidance; an LLM gate can inject a relevant implementation lesson and check suggestion after tool interactions. Agent weights and tools stay fixed.

**What changes:** Memory, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Historical task requirements, trajectories, submissions, and success/failure feedback support lesson extraction and review.

**Evaluation.** Uses shared source trajectories and disjoint test problems across PDEAgent-Bench, KernelBenchX, KernelGenBench-MS, and SWE-bench Science, with gate/level ablations and transfer between kernel benchmarks.

**Boundary.** The study uses one solving backbone and agent setup. Gate ablation changes both selection and generated advice. Memory stays frozen during testing, so results do not demonstrate continual online memory improvement. Kernel acceleration counts all test tasks that are both correct and at least 1.01 times faster, and transfer remains within related kernel tasks.

## Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces

**2026-10-27 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37255)

**Mechanism.** Decomposes regularized return into an interface-specific optimum and policy mismatch under a finite semantic-control model. It tests how presentation or execution changes can alter frozen-model behavior and how further training changes harness rankings.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Task rewards support controlled policy training; sampled actions and stronger-teacher probes estimate deployment mismatch.

**Evaluation.** Uses exact-control MiniWoB++ experiments with six harnesses, adaptation and sampling controls, plus five coding harnesses on Terminal-Bench Lite.

**Boundary.** The theory assumes a specified KL-regularized control problem. Coding-agent ceilings are stronger-teacher proxies sampled on three tasks, not solved optima. Mismatch estimation requires substantial query budgets; observed ranking agreement does not establish universal prediction or autonomous harness optimization.

<a id="obsolete-facts-memory"></a>

## When Retrieval Is Not Enough: Obsolete Facts in Agent Memory

**2026-10-26 · preprint · Author reports PALM workshop at NeurIPS 2026; primary venue record not verified. · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36308)

**Mechanism.** Separates retrieving the newest statement from selecting it correctly. Varies BM25 evidence budgets, then replaces an unrelated statement with an obsolete competitor while keeping the latest statement, reader, prompt, and four-statement count fixed.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** No retained learning update; controlled evidence substitutions and benchmark answers diagnose use of revised facts.

**Evaluation.** Studies single-hop FactConsolidation at 6K and 32K history lengths. A paired 74-question intervention finds stale-answer failures in two Qwen models despite the correction remaining visible.

**Boundary.** Prompt development reused the intervention cohort. Synthetic stale facts often agree with pretrained world knowledge, so chronology alone is not isolated. Gold-assisted support audits are diagnostic; substring scoring has documented errors. Shared histories, short update chains, and one model family limit generalization.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/oleeviyababu/Memory_Conflict) — Paper-linked repository and saved-result inventory inspected; experiments and analysis scripts were not executed.

**Topics:** memory, evaluation, continual-learning. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-04.

## Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10498)

**Mechanism.** Selects informative trials over code/skill hypotheses and retains successful revisions in hierarchical memory. A PPO-trained manager learns memory actions while the robot foundation model and memory operator remain frozen during evolution.

**What changes:** Agent code, Skills, Memory, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Matched execution outcomes, hypothesis uncertainty, experiment cost, and later improvement used to train a memory manager.

**Evaluation.** Reports RoboCasa365 and LIBERO-Pro with disjoint evolution/evaluation seeds, component ablations, and transfer of the simulation-evolved harness to five physical SO-101 tasks.

**Boundary.** “Zero-shot” concerns the harness: the real-robot SmolVLA backbone was first fine-tuned on fifty human demonstrations per task. Thirty trials per condition/task and bounded benchmarks do not establish indefinite retention or improvement of the outer selection procedure.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not established in this source review; nothing was installed or executed.

**Topics:** architecture, skills, memory, model-training, continual-learning, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-30.

## ASCENT: Online Test-Time Training of Long-Horizon Agents via Self-Distillation of Verified Experience

**2026-10-04 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05303)

**Mechanism.** After one scored attempt per task, a frozen copy of the initial model reads accepted experience with hindsight. Its token distributions train persistent LoRA adapters for subsequent tasks; invalid-action turns are removed from the privileged teacher input.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Completed execution trajectories accepted by an environment verifier, with action-validity feedback.

**Evaluation.** The authors report success, interaction cost, ablations, and held-out scene transfer on ALFWorld and WebShop with two model sizes, plus AppWorld experiments.

**Boundary.** The method needs an available verifier and update compute. WebShop adaptation accepts scores of at least 0.9 although reported exact success requires 1.0; outcome acceptance does not identify causally useful actions or prove a shortest solution.

## VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses

**2026-10-02 · preprint · core · paper**

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Skills, Tools, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Executed draft checks, failure replay and perturbation, training regressions, and validation summaries.

**Evaluation.** Adds VERSE to four reimplemented harness optimizers, evaluating held-out SWE-rebench and newer multilingual tasks; also studies Terminal-Bench and component ablations.

## RIFAR: Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay for Continual Robot Learning with World-Action Models

**2026-10-02 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03079)

**Mechanism.** Retains short historical demonstration prefixes, generates replay trajectories and screens their action–visual consistency. After initial new-task adaptation, replay prioritizes reliable trajectories showing greater action drift. Both the policy and reliability model receive staged updates.

**What changes:** Model weights, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** New-task demonstrations, inverse-dynamics consistency of generated replay and action-prediction drift after adaptation.

**Evaluation.** Studies three LIBERO suites and a three-task Franka sequence, comparing retention, acquisition and historical-data storage with real-data and generative replay.

**Boundary.** Relies on demonstrations and fixed task sequences. The v3 reliability model learns from generated replay and can inherit its errors; rollout termination can be premature. Full real-data replay remains stronger on several metrics. Retained-history savings do not measure total training or generation cost.

## SAGE: A Statistical Acceptance Gate for Self-Evolving Agents

**2026-09-28 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36043)

**Mechanism.** Retains skill edits only when paired wins outweigh penalized regressions, an exact binomial test rejects the null, and a regression cap is satisfied. The acting model and edit proposer remain fixed.

**What changes:** Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Binary verifier outcomes for the incumbent and candidate skill on the same validation items.

**Evaluation.** Compares the gate with the same SkillOpt proposer across five benchmarks and four backbones, including component ablations and reported matched proposal/token budgets.

**Boundary.** Error control is per fixed comparison; reuse of validation data does not provide a trajectory-level guarantee. Thresholds still require held-out tuning, and tests assume binary outcomes. Multimodal and multi-agent transfer remain untested.

**2026-09-27 · preprint · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** Allocates a global error budget over possible candidate and promotion histories, accepting updates only after paired tests pass. Audit certificates stay hidden from the proposer; the paper derives simultaneous guarantees under an independent evaluation sample and decision-only feedback.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Paired incumbent-candidate scores on a protected evaluation set; only promotion decisions from that set return to the proposer.

**2026-09-26 · preprint · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** Synthesizes games inside fixed reward and observation templates, checks replay and independent implementations, then distills teacher trajectories into a student. Subsequent student self-play updates its weights using the Crab estimator.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Game-engine outcomes, stronger-teacher self-play traces, and a corpus-informed advantage baseline.

**2026-08-23 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22610)

**Mechanism.** Changes MemSkill's bank-admission score to include sampled joint skill effects while retaining its trained controller. Before deployment, a separate greedy procedure rebuilds target memories and masks skills whose removal improves a retrieval-quality proxy; the retained bank and mask persist.

**What changes:** Skills, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Source outcome rewards and sampled skill-coalition knockout scores; unlabeled target-query retrieval similarity guides transfer masking.

**Evaluation.** Studies LoCoMo, LongMemEval, HotpotQA and ALFWorld with three seeds, coalition audits and six-bank target masking; the gate study covers twelve proposals.

**Boundary.** Evidence concerns one MemSkill-based setup and small banks. The highlighted target-side utility reversal has an interval including zero. Retrieval similarity is a proxy, and masking adds quadratic memory rebuild work before inference. This does not establish online adaptation to changing APIs or general skill compositions.

## When Not to Imitate: Boundary-Aware Skill Memory for Reliable Tool-Use LLM Agents

**2026-08-23 · peer-reviewed · Findings of EMNLP 2026 · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** Builds a reusable skill library with explicit conditions, risk cues and avoidance rules. Retrieval exposes relevant boundaries under a context budget; runtime checks can block or revise tool calls, with local repair hints after failures. Model weights remain fixed.

## CIDER: Continual Interactive Distillation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning

**2026-08-22 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21899)

**Mechanism.** Interleaves online actor-critic learning with distillation from the preceding consolidated policy. Gradient routing separates acquisition and retention updates while producing one shared actor; historical states support distillation rather than old-task Bellman updates.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Current-task rewards, human demonstrations and corrective interventions, plus a frozen prior actor’s action distributions on archived states.

**Evaluation.** Reports sequential acquisition and retention across six real-robot household and industrial manipulation tasks, with evaluation after each stage and gradient-routing, initialization, and sampling ablations.

**Boundary.** This is human-assisted, reward-driven acquisition on short-horizon tasks. Longer tasks with sparse rewards or delayed failures may need additional supervision; the six-task result does not establish unbounded skill accumulation.

## PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents

**2026-06-06 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08106)

**Mechanism.** Places a sequential statistical gate between proposed prompt edits and retention. A betting-based evidence process accepts an edit only after its paired outcomes cross a threshold; otherwise the incumbent remains.

**What changes:** Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Paired candidate/incumbent correctness on development instances.

**Evaluation.** Author experiments use Qwen2.5 prompt evolution on GSM8K, SVAMP, and ARC-Challenge, with planted-gain and stochastic regimes and a separate audit pool. Statistical gates reduce noisy commitments relative to greedy selection.

**Boundary.** The guarantee is per candidate under a conditional paired-null assumption, not a guarantee for the whole adaptive search. Experiments cover one model family and prompt edits; the finite audit and development-set coverage limit interpretation. Small genuine gains may be rejected.

<a id="self-evolution-generalization-gap"></a>

## On the Generalization Gap in Self-Evolving Language Model Reasoning

**2026-05-31 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01075)

**Mechanism.** Compares single-round verification, feedback-guided revision, repeated preference training, and curricula inside a controlled generator-verifier loop. Retained changes are trained policy weights rather than an evolving agent harness.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Preference labels and revision feedback generated by the same base model from supplied unlabeled prompts; oracle labels form comparison arms.

**Evaluation.** Studies easy-to-hard Knights and Knaves reasoning and OpenThoughts-based training with mathematical/generalization tests. Gains often plateau below oracle supervision; a larger-model revision condition nearly closes the gap.

**Boundary.** The restricted offline setup is not an impossibility result for all self-improvement. Open-ended tests cannot isolate verifier error from prompt-distribution shifts, and online-RL comparison rows use different starting models and supervision. Improved pass@1 with nearly unchanged pass@32 limits claims about expanded solution coverage.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not independently verified in this review; no research implementation was executed.

**Topics:** model-training, evaluation, self-play. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-02.

## On Safety Risks in Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Agents

**2026-04-18 · peer-reviewed · Findings of ACL 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16968)

**Mechanism.** Studies safety changes when offline Agent Workflow Memory or online ReasoningBank supplies accumulated experience to frozen models. Varying experience size and a length-matched prompt control probe the contribution of retrieved content.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Benign execution experience and, in mixed-stream experiments, execution or refusal experiences retained by the evaluated frameworks.

**Evaluation.** Tests web and simulated household settings using BrowserART, Agent-SafetyBench, and SafeAgentBench, with several model backbones and mixed benign/harmful experience streams.

**Boundary.** Results cover two frameworks and finite runs up to 800 steps, using automated safety grading. Refusal experience reduces unsafe behavior but can increase over-refusal. Curator interpretation: attribution and prompt controls support a bounded explanation, not universal causality or inevitable failure of every learning agent.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this review; no implementation was installed or executed.

**Topics:** memory, safety, evaluation, continual-learning. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-01.

<a id="combee"></a>

## Combee: Scaling Prompt Learning for Self-Improving Language Model Agents

**2026-04-05 · peer-reviewed · COLM 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04247)

**Mechanism.** Adds a scaling layer to existing generate-reflect-update methods: hierarchical parallel aggregation, duplicated/shuffled reflections, and latency-based batch selection produce reusable context updates without weight training.

**What changes:** Prompts / context, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Textual reflections from task executions, downstream scores, and measured iteration latency.

**Evaluation.** Tests ACE and GEPA on AppWorld, Terminal-Bench, Formula, and FiNER, including held-out tasks, aggregation controls, cost measurements, and selected repeated-run analyses.

**Boundary.** The largest speedup does not preserve identical accuracy: Terminal-Bench Combee scores below sequential ACE. Rare or conflicting reflections can still be lost. The batch controller uses single-trial profiling and a fixed threshold; asynchronous execution and broader framework transfer remain untested.

**Code / data.** Author blog describes ACE/GEPA integrations; a pinned runnable paper implementation was not independently verified or executed.

**Topics:** prompts, workflows, memory, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-01.

<a id="apex-em"></a>

## APEX-EM: Non-Parametric Online Learning for Autonomous Agents via Structured Procedural-Episodic Experience Replay

**2026-03-31 · peer-reviewed · Findings of EMNLP 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29093)

**Mechanism.** Stores procedural-episodic traces in a typed graph and retrieves them by semantic, structural, and graph signals. A plan/retrieve/generate/iterate/ingest loop separates within-task repair from retaining experience without weight updates.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Task verification and teacher-model scores/feedback on completed successful and failed executions.

**Evaluation.** Version 3 evaluates code, structured queries, HLE, Lifelong Agent Bench, and ALFWorld. It distinguishes recurring training tasks from held-out transfer using frozen memory and adds same-backbone comparisons.

**Boundary.** Cumulative success means solved at least once across repeated epochs, not first-attempt generalization. Teacher/verifier feedback and domain adapters remain inputs; cross-backbone reference rows are not controlled comparisons. Monotonic storage growth alone does not establish freedom from forgetting.

**Code / data.** The inspected v3 promises an artifact release; no official repository was verified and no code was executed.

## Hyperagents

**2026-03-19 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461)

**Mechanism.** Combines the task solver and the agent that modifies it in one editable program. DGM-Hyperagents can therefore revise their own improvement procedure as well as task-solving code.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task evaluation and archived improvement histories, including transfer tests for the meta-agent.

**Evaluation.** Studies coding, paper-review prediction, robotics reward design, and math-solution grading. The reviewed v2 separately transfers the task agent and meta agent; meta-only transfer recovers nearly all combined-transfer benefit in its 50-iteration math-grading test.

**Boundary.** The transfer test holds the meta agent fixed while it generates task-agent variants. Initial math graders fail output formatting, affecting the starting score. Main experiments retain fixed task distributions and outer selection/evaluation; bounded transfer does not establish unbounded or self-accelerating improvement.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Hyperagents) — Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.

<a id="exprag"></a>

## Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience

**2026-03-18 · peer-reviewed · EMNLP 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18272)

**Mechanism.** Trains the policy to use full retrieved trajectories instead of adding memory only at inference. The main retrieval bank stays read-only; separate experiments reuse a first attempt as context for a second without parameter updates.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Supervised assistant-token targets from environment trajectories, augmented with retrieved experience during LoRA training.

**Evaluation.** Compares inference-only retrieval and retrieval-aware fine-tuning on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld, including easy-to-hard task-group transfer, retrieval ablations, and imperfect or self-generated experience.

**Boundary.** Main hard-task evaluations retrieve matched hard-task expert traces despite easy-only policy training. Self-experience covers one retry and hurts ScienceWorld despite helping ALFWorld. Cross-paper headline comparisons are qualitative; long-term heterogeneous memory accumulation is not evaluated.

## MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks

**2026-02-18 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16313)

**Mechanism.** Constructs multi-session tasks in which earlier choices and discoveries constrain later execution. Persistent memory connects sessions; comparisons separate long-context history, external memory systems, and retrieval-based stores.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Earlier task actions and observations supply experience needed for later dependent subtasks.

**Mechanism.** Alternates bounded reasoning attempts with summary updates for the same problem. GRPO trains summary-conditioned generation, and a replay buffer supplies later-turn summaries; inference expands the reasoning budget without updating weights.

**2026-01-08 · preprint · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** A fixed development engine generates diagnostic scripts and one prompt/code/tool-wrapper release candidate per iteration. A configurable regression gate retains accepted blueprints; the same development set drives diagnosis, promotion and stopping.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Programmatic scores or an implementation-blind LLM critic, trace-derived symptoms, and development-set pass-to-fail/fail-to-pass changes.

WebArena final scores differ between Table 1 (35.5) and Table 3 (34.2) without an explicit reconciliation. ## Temporal Self-Rewarding Language Models: Decoupling Chosen-Rejected via Past-Future

**2026 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/wang26ik.html)

**Mechanism.** Separates the model generations used to provide rejected and chosen samples so their learning signal does not shrink as both improve together. The paper applies this temporal arrangement to iterative self-rewarding training.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Preferences using anchored past-model rejections and newer-model chosen responses.

**Evaluation.** The authors compare model families and sizes at matched compute and report instruction-following and selected out-of-distribution reasoning, QA, and coding results.

## SkillRubricsRL: Evolving Skill-Grounded Agents with Rubric-Guided Reinforcement Learning

**2026 · peer-reviewed · Findings of EMNLP 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-emnlp.471/)

**Mechanism.** Pairs each skill with execution criteria, trains an acting policy with combined outcome and fulfillment rewards, and evolves the skill bank from failures. Marginal utility guides retrieval; later mixed skill-on/off training encourages behavior that persists without prompt-time skills.

**What changes:** Model weights, Skills, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment rewards and model-judged skill-fulfillment rubrics train the policy; perturbed-skill rollout outcomes update retrieval utilities.

**Evaluation.** Evaluates ALFWorld and WebShop, component ablations, skill-on/off deployment and a small human agreement check of the rubric judge.

**Boundary.** Best reported metrics come from different skill-on/off conditions. Utility probes give marginal effects, not complete interaction attribution. The cost table excludes actor training, local rollouts and one external model's charges. The inspected repository remains a placeholder.

## PerMemSafe: Benchmarking Implicit Personalized Safety of Long Horizon Self-Evolving Agents

**2026 · peer-reviewed · Findings of ACL 2026 · adjacent · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.320/)

**Mechanism.** Separates recognizing implicit personalized risks from tracking their changes over time. The accompanying SentinelMem retains explicit fact-state transitions and separates preference information from safety constraints.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Changing implicit user-risk cues in constructed multi-session conversations, with annotated safety contexts for evaluation.

**Evaluation.** Compares full-context models and five memory frameworks on safety perception and dynamic evolution, scoring retrieval, personalized response safety, and helpfulness; model grading is checked against a human sample.

**2025-11-03 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2026 · adjacent · paper**

**Mechanism.** One model plays solver and reframer roles, pooling answer frequencies with a harmonic-mean selector. Reinforcement learning updates shared model parameters from original-solution and fused reframe-and-solve trajectories; each benchmark gets its own adapted model.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Agreement among model answers to original and reframed questions supplies pseudo-labels, with format/diversity reward terms.

## Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs

**2025-08-22 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.16153)

**Mechanism.** A planner-executor agent stores completed cases and reuses them in subsequent planning. Retrieval can use fixed similarity or a learned Q-function; underlying LLM weights remain frozen, while the optional retrieval network changes.

**What changes:** Memory, Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Task outcomes attached to stored plans; the parametric variant trains a separate case-selection network from binary success feedback.

**Evaluation.** Reports deep-research and QA evaluations, memory ablations, and transfer. GAIA validation accumulates cases over three passes; the test run uses the validation-built case bank.

**Boundary.** Validation Pass@3 and test accuracy use different protocols. The parametric variant performs gradient updates outside the LLM, so the whole system should not be described as parameter-free. Long-horizon Level 3 tasks remain difficult.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/Memento-Teams/Memento) — The author-linked Agent-on-the-Fly repository redirects to Memento-Teams/Memento; public page inspected, not executed.

**Topics:** memory, continual-learning, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-29.

<a id="mem0"></a>

## Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory

**2025-04-28 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19413)

**Mechanism.** Extracts facts from recent exchanges and background summaries, then updates an external memory store through add/update/delete/no-op decisions. The graph variant stores entities and relations and can invalidate obsolete edges; neither variant trains model weights during memory management.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Conversation messages, summaries and LLM decisions about whether candidate facts add, update, contradict or duplicate stored information.

**Evaluation.** LoCoMo conversational QA excluding adversarial questions, with lexical metrics, repeated judge scoring and query-time latency/token measurements. The full-context baseline has higher overall judge accuracy; graph memory helps some categories but trails base Mem0 on single- and multi-hop questions.

**Boundary.** Query-time savings do not include the full cost of building and updating memory. Hosted/manual baselines and imported results require version-matched protocols; A-MEM category labels differ across the compared documents. The permissive judge and exclusion of unanswerable questions limit factuality/abstention conclusions. Production readiness is not independently established.

**Code / data.** Code availability not verified in this review.

**Topics:** memory, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

**2025-01-20 · preprint · core · paper**

## LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory

**2024-10-14 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · adjacent · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813)

**Mechanism.** Constructs 500 curated questions with annotated evidence embedded in scalable user-assistant histories, testing extraction, multi-session reasoning, updates, temporal reasoning and abstention. It separates indexing, retrieval and reading, then varies their designs without training a continually improving policy.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.

**Evaluation.** Studies roughly 115k-token and 1.5M-token histories, retrieval granularity, fact-expanded keys, temporal filters and reader prompts. A GPT-4o judge is checked against humans on thirty responses per question type from each of two answer models; retrieval and answer scores are reported separately.

**Boundary.** Histories combine simulated/human-edited evidence with sampled background sessions. The 97-question commercial-system study used shorter histories in August 2024 and omitted several abilities. Reader and query-model choices affect gains; retrieval correctness can require obsolete evidence unnecessary for a correct updated answer. Recall scores do not establish procedural learning.

## AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation

**2024-10-14 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10762)

**Mechanism.** Searches over code-represented workflows using a Monte Carlo tree-search variant. An LLM changes prompts and connections between operations, while the tree retains feedback from prior candidates.

**What changes:** Workflows, Prompts / context, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Execution scores on a validation subset and stored search experience.

**Evaluation.** Six QA, coding, and math datasets are divided into development and test subsets; the paper also compares execution costs and transfer between executor models.

**Boundary.** The study focuses on reasoning tasks with accessible evaluators and commonly used operators. Search costs and repeated validation exposure should be considered separately from the inference cost of the selected workflow.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/FoundationAgents/AFlow) — Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.

**Topics:** workflows, architecture, prompts. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

<a id="agentsquare"></a>

## AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space

**2024-10-08 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06153)

**Mechanism.** Alternates code-level module evolution with recombination of planning, reasoning, tool-use and memory modules. Novel modules receive environment evaluation; recombinations use an LLM surrogate. Module pools and scored designs persist within a fixed external search procedure.

**What changes:** Workflows, Prompts / context, Tools, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task-performance evaluations and an in-context predictor conditioned on examples of previously evaluated module combinations.

**Evaluation.** GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o comparisons on WebShop, ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, M3ToolEval, TravelPlanner and PDDL, with module ablations, surrogate-versus-observed plots and search/execution-cost analyses. Reported metrics differ across tasks: success, reward, progress and micro pass rate.

**Boundary.** Search remains constrained by standardized interfaces. Execution-cost plots exclude search costs, which are tabulated separately. The inspected paper does not specify a separate held-out search/test partition or independent-run uncertainty; surrogate correlation is not a guarantee that novel designs generalize.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/AgentSquare) — Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.

**Topics:** architecture, workflows, memory, tools. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning

**2024-09-19 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12917)

**Mechanism.** Trains a correction policy on its own response distribution, with an initialization stage and a reward bonus encouraging successful revision. The method targets distribution mismatch and collapsed correction behavior observed in offline supervised training.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Online rewards and regularization over self-generated multi-turn correction traces.

**Evaluation.** The authors evaluate self-correction on MATH and HumanEval using Gemini models.

**Boundary.** The training produces a reusable correction capability; a test-time revision is still a within-problem operation. Curator interpretation: these benchmarks do not show autonomous lifelong improvement across changing environments.

**2024-09-11 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07429)

**Mechanism.** Abstracts reusable subroutines from action trajectories and adds them to the agent context as workflow memory. It supports an offline store built from training examples and an online store updated after completed tasks.

**What changes:** Memory, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Annotated offline trajectories or model-judged successful online task trajectories.

## Automated Design of Agentic Systems

**2024-08-15 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08435)

**Mechanism.** A fixed meta-agent writes executable forward functions, checks novelty, repairs execution errors, and archives designs with scores. Search changes prompts and control flow in task agents; the outer search algorithm and model weights are fixed.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Validation-task scores, runtime errors and an archive of earlier code designs; the pretrained meta-agent proposes and reflects on candidates.

**Evaluation.** ARC grid-transformation code and DROP, MGSM, MMLU and GPQA; cross-domain/model transfer and empty-archive controls. ARC uses 20 validation and 60 test problems with grids at most 5 by 5; reported intervals are bootstrap estimates, not independent search-run variation.

**Boundary.** Experiments concern bounded question-answering tasks; continual deployment and optimization of the meta-agent are proposed future work. ARC transfer candidates were selected by source test accuracy. Transfer does not benefit every agent/model pairing, and performance-only search does not establish equal-cost superiority.

**2024-07-25 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2024 · core · paper**

## AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data

**2024-07-24 · peer-reviewed · Nature 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07566-y)

**Mechanism.** Analyzes how repeated training on generated data can lose low-probability parts of an original distribution and amplify errors. The paper combines tractable distribution models with generative-model experiments.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Recursive resampling and training on prior-generation model outputs.

**Evaluation.** Experiments include Gaussian mixtures, variational autoencoders, and repeated language-model fine-tuning, with differing amounts of original data retained.

**Boundary.** The theoretical replacement setting and finite experiments have specific data-mixing assumptions. Curator interpretation: this is a warning about recursive data use, not a proof that every verified or data-accumulating self-learning loop must fail.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**2024-04-01 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01413)

**Mechanism.** Compares replacement of earlier datasets with accumulation of original and synthetic data. It supplies a linear-model analysis and generative-model experiments showing that the data-retention policy changes collapse behavior.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Repeated generated-data training with old data retained rather than replaced.

**Evaluation.** The study includes small transformer language models on TinyStories, molecular diffusion, image variational autoencoders, and controlled analytical models.

**Boundary.** The bounded-error theorem is for its stated linear setting, and retaining growing datasets changes resource requirements. Curator interpretation: these results challenge universal collapse claims without certifying arbitrary self-training or agent-memory loops.

## MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

**2023-10-12 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560)

**Mechanism.** Separates active context from archival and recall storage. Function calls page information in and out, edit working memory, and request successive inference steps; persistent records support later conversations without changing model weights.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Conversation history, retrieved documents, memory-pressure notices and function outcomes guide a frozen model in choosing memory edits and searches.

**Evaluation.** Augmented Multi-Session Chat tests recall and persona-based opening messages; document QA uses 50 NaturalQuestions questions, and synthetic nested-key retrieval varies nesting with 30 orderings. GPT-4-based memory retrieval improves over summary-only chat baselines; function-calling ability affects results.

**Boundary.** Chat baselines see lossy summaries while MemGPT can search full history, with different answer instructions. The recall judge is permissive; engagement is measured by similarity, not demonstrated user satisfaction. Limited benchmark horizons and premature search stopping do not establish reliable unlimited memory or reusable procedural learning.

## DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines

**2023-10-05 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2024 · adjacent · paper**

**Mechanism.** Compiles declarative LM modules by bootstrapping and selecting demonstrations. Composed optimizers can ensemble programs or fine-tune smaller models. Optimized prompts, program configurations or weights persist, while the developer supplies the task decomposition and metric.

**What changes:** Prompts / context, Workflows, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Developer-defined metrics and training examples filter generated execution traces; optional teacher programs supply intermediate demonstrations or fine-tuning targets.

**Evaluation.** GSM8K and HotpotQA comparisons cover prompting, bootstrapping, ensembles and T5 distillation. **Boundary.** External compilation is not autonomous continual learning. Development and test numbers are distinct; the T5 distillation result is development-only. Ensembles and search add computation, and strong teachers or answer labels remain inputs. This review concerns the original v1 paper, not every feature of current DSPy.

## Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation

**2023-10-03 · peer-reviewed · COLM 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02304)

**Mechanism.** Begins with an LLM-assisted program improver and applies that improver to its own source. Candidate improvers are assessed through the quality of programs they generate for downstream tasks.

**What changes:** Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Utility functions scoring the programs produced by an improver.

**Evaluation.** The study reports improvements on a small set of algorithmic tasks and separately examines attempts to bypass a sandbox.

**Boundary.** The authors explicitly retain a fixed language model, so the result is bounded scaffold self-improvement. Performance on the small task set does not establish an indefinitely accelerating process.

## RoboCat: A Self-Improving Generalist Agent for Robotic Manipulation

**2023-06-20 · peer-reviewed · TMLR 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11706)

**Mechanism.** Fine-tunes a visual goal-conditioned generalist into task-specific policies, collects additional trajectories with them, then retrains a generalist on old and new data. Reusable improvement resides in model weights rather than an expanding executable skill library.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Human demonstrations, goal-relabeled robot trajectories, and learned success detectors used during data collection.

**Evaluation.** Reports simulation and real-robot manipulation across embodiments, adaptation to new tasks, and an isolated comparison of demonstrations alone versus demonstrations plus self-generated data.

## MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory

**2023-05-17 · peer-reviewed · AAAI 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10250)

**Mechanism.** Stores dialogue records, daily/global summaries and user profiles, retrieves them with dense embeddings, and proposes exponential time decay with stronger retention after recall. SiliconFriend separately LoRA-tunes open models on 38,000 psychological dialogues before integrating memory.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Past conversations, generated event/personality summaries, elapsed time and recall frequency shape stored context and proposed memory retention.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v3 reports 194 manually written questions over ten simulated days for fifteen synthetic users, split equally between English and Chinese. Human ratings compare three SiliconFriend backbones on retrieval, correctness and coherence; real-user examples illustrate recall and personalization.

**Boundary.** The quantitative study does not isolate the forgetting rule or compare memory versus no-memory under a matched backbone. Synthetic probes and selected empathy examples are not clinical validation or general skill learning. The reviewed body is arXiv v3; current AAAI body access was restricted, so publication-version equivalence is not assumed.

**Code / data.** Code availability not verified in this review.

**Topics:** foundations, memory. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="generative-agents"></a>

## Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

**2023-04-07 · peer-reviewed · UIST 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442)

**Mechanism.** Stores observations, plans and recursive reflections in a persistent memory stream. Recency, importance and embedding relevance determine retrieval; a frozen language model generates plans, dialogue and reactions from that context.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Observed sandbox events, model-scored memory importance and model-generated reflections influence later retrieval and plans; identities and initial goals are human-authored.

**Evaluation.** Twenty-five agents interact for two simulated days. One hundred evaluators rank interview responses from the full architecture, ablations and crowdworker-written baselines. Ablations reuse histories generated by the full system; separate descriptive analyses examine information diffusion, relationships and party attendance.

**Boundary.** Believability is not factual accuracy or increasing task competence. Ablations do not independently rerun the social simulation, and the human baseline is not expert performance. Retrieval failures, embellished memories, over-cooperation, simulation cost and short observation horizons limit claims of reliable lifelong learning.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/joonspk-research/generative_agents) — Official repository inspected on 2026-10-28; not executed. UIST 2023 publication is verified from the official proceedings; the earlier ACM access limitation is retained in the review history.

**Topics:** foundations, memory, architecture. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback

**2023-03-30 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651)

**Mechanism.** Alternates drafting, feedback and revision while retaining the current task history. No weights or cross-task memory are updated; stopping and output selection vary across the evaluated tasks.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** within-task. **Learning signal:** The same model generates task-specific critiques using curated few-shot examples; separate oracle experiments additionally use answer correctness to control refinement.

**Evaluation.** Seven text/code tasks with automatic measures, model preferences and blinded author assessments; feedback ablations, repeated-sampling controls and weaker-model analysis. Main-table math gains are only 0–0.2 percentage points. Oracle-guided math results in Appendices H/O are a different setting.

**Boundary.** The headline average combines heterogeneous metrics and is not a universal accuracy gain. Prompt examples include human-written feedback and revisions. Quality can regress and weaker models fail to refine. Appendix J labels its intervals 95% in the caption and 99% in the text, leaving their confidence level ambiguous.

**Code / data.** No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.

<a id="toolformer"></a>

## Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

**2023-02-09 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2023 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761)

**Mechanism.** Samples API calls into ordinary text, executes and filters them using future-token loss reduction, and fine-tunes GPT-J on the augmented corpus. Learned tool invocation persists in weights; the tool set and data-selection heuristics remain fixed.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Human-seeded API examples propose calls; tool responses are retained when they reduce loss on subsequent corpus tokens, then become fine-tuning data.

**Evaluation.** LAMA, arithmetic, QA, multilingual and temporal tasks, plus language-model perplexity and size/decoding analyses. Gains vary by task: QA remains below GPT-3, and some multilingual results regress relative to GPT-J. Evaluation allows at most one call and encourages it when the API token is among the top ten.

**Boundary.** Training calls are sampled independently, so chained or interactive tool use is not learned. Benchmarks selectively disable tools and use relaxed answer matching. Tool costs are not optimized; API outputs can be noisy, and externally supplied QA/translation models contribute capability. Zero-shot downstream evaluation is not zero-demonstration training.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** foundations, tools, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="constitutional-ai"></a>

## Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

**2022-12-15 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073)

**Mechanism.** Fine-tunes on constitution-guided response revisions, then fits a preference model to mixed human-helpfulness and AI-harmlessness labels and trains a policy with RL. Learned weights persist; the constitution, training procedure and evaluation rules are externally chosen.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Human-written principles and few-shot examples guide AI critiques and harmlessness comparisons; human helpfulness preference labels and human/model-generated prompts remain training inputs.

**Evaluation.** Crowdworker comparisons assess helpfulness and harmlessness across model sizes and training snapshots, alongside critique/revision controls, AI-label evaluations and a learned harmfulness scorer. Evaluators explicitly prefer non-evasive answers when similarly harmless, unlike the earlier baseline-labeling instructions.

**Boundary.** This removes human harmlessness preference labels, not all human supervision. Over-training can produce boilerplate and overly harsh replies; critiques can be inaccurate. Different initialization and feedback-model choices complicate isolated component attribution, and finite red-team evaluations do not guarantee safety under later self-modification.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** foundations, model-training, safety. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="react"></a>

## ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

**2022-10-06 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)

**Mechanism.** Interleaves language reasoning, tool actions and observations to revise a plan within a task. The main prompted variant keeps weights fixed; the separately evaluated fine-tuned variant retains learned weights across tasks.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Environment observations guide the prompted task loop; a separate offline experiment uses 3,000 answer-correct generated trajectories to fine-tune smaller models.

**Evaluation.** HotpotQA, FEVER, 134 ALFWorld games and 500 WebShop instructions, with reasoning-only/action-only controls and fine-tuning comparisons. ReAct alone trails CoT on HotpotQA; hybrids perform better. The headline ALFWorld result is the best of six prompt configurations, distinct from their mean.

**Boundary.** Prompted interaction does not itself retain learning between tasks. Human-authored demonstrations and external retrieval support performance; retrieval failures and reasoning loops remain. Offline fine-tuning is distinct from self-directed online improvement, and interpretable traces do not guarantee faithful reasoning.

**Code / data.** No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.

**Topics:** foundations, tools. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

**2022-03-28 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2022 · adjacent · paper**

**Mechanism.** Generates reasoning traces, keeps traces ending in the reference answer, and fine-tunes on them. Failed problems can be retried with the answer supplied as a hint; each outer iteration retrains from the original base model on the newly collected traces.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Known correct answers filter generated rationales; answer hints support rationalization of failed examples.

**Evaluation.** Experiments cover arithmetic, CommonsenseQA, and GSM8K, with comparisons to direct-answer fine-tuning and prompted reasoning.

**Boundary.** The method needs training questions, reference answers, and a small rationale seed. Correct final answers do not independently certify that every intermediate explanation is valid.

<a id="alphago-zero"></a>

## Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge

**2017-10-19 · peer-reviewed · Nature 2017 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature24270)

**Mechanism.** Alternates search-guided self-play with gradient updates to a shared policy/value network. Recent games are replayed to fit improved move distributions and outcomes. The training/search algorithm and network design remain externally specified.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** MCTS visit distributions and scored self-play outcomes train a policy/value network; a 400-game comparison gate admits new data-generating checkpoints above 55% wins.

**Evaluation.** The 3-day, 20-block run generated 4.9 million games and defeated AlphaGo Lee 100–0; a separate 40-day, 40-block run generated 29 million games and defeated AlphaGo Master 89–11. Architecture controls use fixed self-play data, and move prediction differs from playing strength.

**Boundary.** No human game demonstrations are used for the principal training runs, but exact rules, legal moves, board symmetries, architecture and search-parameter tuning remain inputs. Four TPUs describe the playing configuration, not total training compute; optimization used 64 GPU workers and 19 CPU parameter servers. Evidence is specific to Go.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** foundations, self-play, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.
